mainEntity.name: How long do I need to wait before replacing a failed implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The waiting period typically ranges from three to six months after implant removal, allowing adequate healing time. If bone grafting is required, the timeline may extend to six to twelve months. Your dental professional will assess healing progress and determine the optimal timing for replacement based on your individual case.

mainEntity.name: Are replacement implants more likely to fail than original implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacement implants can achieve similar success rates to original implants when the cause of failure is properly identified and addressed. Success depends on factors such as bone quality, overall health, and compliance with post-operative care. Careful treatment planning and addressing underlying issues can actually improve outcomes for replacement procedures.

mainEntity.name: Will insurance cover the cost of implant replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Insurance coverage for implant replacement varies depending on your policy and the circumstances of the failure. Some policies may provide coverage if the failure occurs within a certain timeframe or due to specific causes. It's advisable to check with your insurance provider and dental practice about coverage options and payment plans.

mainEntity.name: Can multiple failed implants be replaced at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiple implant replacements can often be performed simultaneously, depending on the location of the failed implants and the condition of the surrounding tissues. Your dental professional will assess each site individually and develop a treatment plan that optimises healing and success whilst minimising the number of surgical procedures required.

mainEntity.name: What are the warning signs that an implant might be failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Warning signs include persistent pain or discomfort, swelling or bleeding around the implant, looseness of the crown or implant itself, changes in bite, or visible changes in the gum tissue around the implant. Any of these symptoms warrant prompt professional evaluation to assess the implant's condition and determine appropriate treatment.

mainEntity.name: How can I improve my chances of successful implant replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Improving replacement success involves maintaining excellent oral hygiene, following all post-operative instructions, avoiding smoking, managing any systemic health conditions, attending regular dental appointments, and protecting implants from excessive force. Addressing the factors that contributed to the original failure is essential for long-term success.
